dependencies.reason: Supplies the Warning{code, severity, stage, message} shape the warning event mirrors verbatim, and the envelope's status vocabulary run_end.status is read from.

Not read from directly by this scope, but run_end's eventual report_file field (added later by envelope_output_file) extends the run_end type this scope defines, so that type's shape here must leave room for it.

tasks.title: Define the closed event envelope and the JSONL sink's serialization core
steps: Write TS-07-7 through TS-07-11 and confirm they fail

Create internal/toolio/events.go defining the closed set of type constants (run_start, step, phase_start, turn, tool_call, check, phase_end, warning, heartbeat, run_end, text) and one Go struct per type carrying only that type's documented fields plus the shared ts/tool/type envelope, so a type never carries a field it does not document

Implement an eventsSink type (a mutex, the tool name, zero or more active io.Writer destinations, an active flag) with an Emit(evt) method that stamps ts as time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339) and tool, marshals the event as one line of compact JSON with no embedded newline, and writes it to every active writer

Make every exported method on eventsSink nil-safe and a no-op when the sink is nil or inactive, mirroring Progress's existing nil-receiver pattern, so that with neither --events jsonl nor --events-file active no event object is ever produced

Add the property test asserting each emitted event type's JSON carries exactly its documented fields (no field belonging to another type) and the unit test asserting a multi-line formatted message still serializes onto a single line

tasks.title: Add --events and --events-file flags and wire the sink into App
steps: Write TS-07-1 through TS-07-6 and confirm they fail
Add Events and EventsFile string fields to toolio.Common and register --events (default "text") and --events-file alongside the rest of the shared flags in Common.Register

In App.Main, right after SplitArgs succeeds and before the --version check, the bare-invocation check, or anything is fetched, validate common.Events is "text" or "jsonl"; on any other value return Emit(stdout, run.Envelope(ExitUsage, nil, &ErrorInfo{Stage: "usage", Category: "usage", Message: ...})) without opening a file or emitting any event
When --events-file names a path, open it once with O_CREATE|O_TRUNC|O_WRONLY and construct the events.go sink from task 1 with that file writer always active, independent of --events
Make the sink's stderr writer active only when common.Events == "jsonl" and !common.Quiet, while the file writer, when present, always carries the full JSONL stream regardless of --events or --quiet
Pass the constructed sink into NewProgress (extend its constructor or add a setter) so Progress can reach it
Write each JSONL line with a single Write call per line, so a process killed mid-run leaves the file as a valid prefix with no partial or corrupted line

Add the integration tests confirming --quiet suppresses stderr under both --events values without affecting the events file, and that a cancelled run leaves the file's already-flushed lines all individually valid JSON

tasks.title: Emit run_start and run_end from the shared shell
steps: Write TS-07-12 through TS-07-16 and confirm they fail

In App.execute, right after e.run.SetModel(...) and e.progress.Detail("model: …") and before agentrun.Config/Runner is built, emit a run_start event {input_kind: in.Kind.String(), model: {spec, id, vendor}} through the sink

In App.Main, immediately before calling Emit(stdout, run.Envelope(...)), emit a run_end event {status, exit_code} derived from the same exit code that decides Envelope.OK, on every path that reaches that call
Confirm neither event fires on the -h/--help path or the bare-invocation path, both of which already return before reaching that point
Confirm run_start (when it fires at all) is always the first event of a run and run_end is always its last event, across ExitOK, ExitFailed, ExitUsage, ExitNeedsHuman and ExitUnverified
Add the property test iterating every one of those exit codes to lock in that run_end.status never disagrees with the envelope's own ok field

tasks.title: Give Progress a JSONL sink behind Step/Begin/Detail/Raw/Check and the Observer methods
steps: Write TS-07-17 through TS-07-25 and confirm they fail

Add a leading `stage string` parameter to Progress.Step; update every call site in codefix/pipeline.go, codeimpl/pipeline.go, codeimpl/gate.go, issuetriage/pipeline.go and specgen/pipeline.go to pass a stage drawn from the same vocabulary Result.Stage/Failure.Stage already use, leaving the printed "[tool] message" line unchanged
Give Progress a reference to the events sink built in tasks 1-2 (set by NewProgress); have Step also emit a step event {stage, message} when the sink is active
Make Progress.Begin print nothing and return a no-op end function when the sink is active, unchanged on a terminal or under --verbose text output otherwise
Leave Detail exactly as it is today: verbose stderr text only, never touching the sink under any --events value

Add PhaseStart, PhaseEnd, Turn and ToolCall method signatures to the agentrun.Observer interface in internal/agentrun/phase.go, and implement all four on *Progress: PhaseStart/PhaseEnd record the current phase name and emit phase_start/phase_end when the sink is active; Turn emits a turn event; ToolCall emits a tool_call event only when Progress.Verbose() is true
Change Progress.Raw to emit a text event {phase: currentPhase, delta: s} instead of writing prose when the sink is active and ShowText is true, and to remain a no-op, as today, when ShowText is false

Add Progress.Check(res checks.Result), emitting a check event {command, ok, exit_code, duration_ms} when the sink is active and doing nothing otherwise; call it immediately after checks.Run returns at codefix.runChecks and codeimpl.runGate
Add `var _ agentrun.Observer = (*toolio.Progress)(nil)` to a test file to lock in interface satisfaction

tasks.title: Wire Runner and Guard to call the new Observer hooks, and give Phase a Task label
steps: Write TS-07-26 through TS-07-32, using a fake Observer that records its calls, and confirm they fail

Add an optional Task string field to agentrun.Phase; set it only at codeimpl's per-task construction of the implement Phase in codeimpl/phases.go's Implement method (e.g. from taskInput.Task's id), leaving Task empty at every other Phase literal in the tree
In Runner.Run, call r.cfg.Observer.PhaseStart(p.Name, p.Task, r.cfg.Bounds.maxTurns(), r.cfg.Bounds.maxBudget()) exactly once before newAgent is built, nil-safe when Observer is nil

As Runner.Run returns, call Observer.PhaseEnd(p.Name, string(res.StopReason), out.Turns, out.Usage.CostUSD, out.Elapsed.Milliseconds()) exactly once, from the same Result already assembled, on both the success and the error return paths

Add a per-phase turn counter inside Runner.Run and call Observer.Turn(p.Name, turn, costUSD, inputTokens, outputTokens) once per turn boundary Runner.trace observes in the phase's event stream, checking the vendored agentkit-go/core package for a per-turn usage event and degrading to zeroed cost/token fields when none exists

Extend Runner.trace's core.ToolCallEndEvent case to call Observer.ToolCall(p.Name, v.Block.Name, false) only when the Observer also satisfies an optional `interface{ Verbose() bool }` and reports true
Change GuardOptions.OnBlock in internal/agentrun/guard.go to carry the tool name separately from the reason (func(name, reason string)), updating guard.go's block() helper and its call sites
In Runner.newAgent's GuardOptions.OnBlock closure, keep counter.inc() and r.detail(...) unchanged, and add a call to Observer.ToolCall(p.Name, name, true) when Verbose() is true
Confirm that with Progress.Verbose() false, neither Runner.trace's ToolCallEndEvent handling nor Guard's OnBlock ever calls Observer.ToolCall

tasks.title: Mirror Run.Warn into warning events through the attached sink
steps: Write TS-07-33 through TS-07-36 and confirm they fail

Add an unexported events-sink field to *toolio.Run and an AttachEvents(sink) setter; call it exactly once in App.Main immediately after run and progress are constructed, passing the same sink instance backing progress

Extend Run.Warn to also emit a warning event {code, severity, stage, message} through the attached sink, using the same code/severity/stage/message the warning is recorded with, whenever a sink is attached and active
Keep Run.Warn nil-safe and panic-free; confirm a bare *Run built via NewRun with no attached sink still records into Warnings() without emitting anything
Add the property test comparing every emitted warning event, field by field, against the matching entry in run.Envelope(...).Warnings for a batch of varied warnings

tasks.title: Run a 15-second heartbeat ticker off the run's own accumulated cost
steps: Write TS-07-37 through TS-07-41, using an injectable clock/interval so 15 seconds do not have to be slept for real, and confirm they fail

Add one heartbeat ticker to the events sink from task 1, started once App.Main activates it (--events jsonl or --events-file), checking on a 1-second interval whether 15 seconds have passed since the last event of any type — run_start counting as the first, a heartbeat as the reset for the next

Track the sink's last-known stage from the most recent step or phase_start event, and read cost_usd from *toolio.Run's existing running phase total (add a small accessor if none exists) rather than computing it a second way
When 15 seconds of silence elapse, emit heartbeat {stage, elapsed_ms, cost_usd}; when any other event is emitted first, reset the window from that event's own timestamp instead of emitting one
Stop the ticker the moment run_end is emitted in App.Main (task 3), so no heartbeat can follow it
Make the ticker's interval and clock source injectable so tests advance a fake clock instead of sleeping real seconds
